prompt: For a maths test covering three problem types, which practice schedule usually produces better performance on mixed test questions?

options.text: Practise type A for a week, then B for a week, then C for a week, never mixing
Practise only the type that feels easiest, to build confidence
Practise each type once, in the order they were taught
Mix the three types within each session, so every problem first requires choosing which method applies

explanation: Blocked practice lets you repeat a method without recognising when to use it. Interleaving forces that recognition step, which is exactly what a mixed test demands.
